raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Gemma KV-sharing readers reuse the writer's cache layer ID. Loading their absent/default scales after the writer currently overwrites its calibrated NVFP4 pool scales with 1.0. This patch keeps scale ownership with the cache writer.

## Modifications

Skip attention modules marked `is_kv_shared_layer` during pool scale initialization. This is a three-line production change; ordinary layers, legitimate calibrated overrides, existing SM100 conversion, and uncalibrated writer defaults retain their behavior. Add an existing-suite CPU regression covering both traversal orders, absent/default/unrelated reader scales, and both SM100 conversion policies.

## Accuracy Tests

On upstream `6e8f3e09dd03a95e9a903d940427d007427bff47`, candidate `4025d6b7911c58643fd23769fe8ccc436251219d`:

- Full registered quantization file: **23 passed, 1 CUDA-only skipped, 16 subtests passed**, using an isolated Python 3.12 environment installed from the current `python/pyproject.toml` (torch 2.14.1, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1). Stock fails eight writer-first regression subcases.
- Architecture/checkpoint-scalar integration: instantiate real Gemma4Attention modules from the original calibrated Gemma-4-E2B checkpoint configuration on meta, load its actual scalar tensors through the real name remapper/default weight loader, and initialize CPU pool scale arrays. Stock matches **0/20** sharing readers against the writer-only control; patched matches **20/20**, with both pool tensors identical to the control.

The integration smoke includes a separately reviewed scalar-float4 checkpoint-loading candidate (`e0f9675741de1619987275053f65168c7f2a5e9a`); current upstream otherwise ignores that checkpoint's scheme. That prerequisite is not included in this PR. The smoke loads checkpoint scalars, not model projection weights, and runs no model forward, CUDA kernels, or generation. It establishes scale ownership, not general quality parity.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-loop work added; the skip runs once during scale initialization. No performance claim or timing benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). All configured hooks applicable to both changed files passed. Guide-required `--all-files` was also attempted in a disposable checkout: baseline end-of-file fixes and Windows Rust `libc::shm` compilation errors prevent a repository-wide pass; unrelated files were not changed in this PR.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No public interface change; ownership comment added.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Bounded scale tests above; no full-model quality or speed benchmarks.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Implementation and validation were performed with OpenAI Codex under the user-authorized task. The commit retains the author's DCO sign-off and discloses AI co-authorship. Human maintainer review remains pending.

## Review and Merge Process

Maintainer review, required CI, and normal CODEOWNERS approval remain pending.

+    def test_scale_loading_uses_writer_for_shared_cache(self):
+        """A shared reader must not overwrite its cache writer's global scales."""
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_kv_cache_quant_method import (
+            NVFP4KVCacheMethod,

+
+        for is_sm100 in (False, True):
+            for writer_scale, reader_scale in (
+                (0.25, None),
+                (0.25, 1.0),
+                (0.25, 9.0),
+                (1.0, 9.0),
+            ):
+                for reader_first in (False, True):
+                    with self.subTest(
+                        is_sm100=is_sm100,
+                        writer_scale=writer_scale,
+                        reader_scale=reader_scale,
+                        reader_first=reader_first,
+                    ):
+                        writer = SimpleNamespace(
+                            self_attn=SimpleNamespace(
+                                is_kv_shared_layer=False,
+                                attn=SimpleNamespace(
+                                    layer_id=2,
+                                    k_scale=torch.tensor(writer_scale),
+                                    v_scale=torch.tensor(writer_scale * 2),
+                                ),
+                            )
+                        )
+                        reader = SimpleNamespace(
+                            self_attn=SimpleNamespace(
+                                is_kv_shared_layer=True,
+                                attn=SimpleNamespace(
+                                    layer_id=2,
+                                    k_scale=(

+                                        if reader_scale is None
+                                        else torch.tensor(reader_scale)
+                                    ),
+                                    v_scale=(

+                                        if reader_scale is None
+                                        else torch.tensor(reader_scale)
+                                    ),
+                                ),
+                            )
+                        )

+                            if reader_first

+                            return_value=SimpleNamespace(is_sm100=is_sm100),

+                            method.load_scales_from_model(model)
+                        expected = tuple(

+                            for scale in (writer_scale, writer_scale * 2)
+                        )
